paragraphs: If you are willing to study a district's public needs and turn population, road network, and land data into verifiable reasons for a choice, it is worth trying first; liking the look of urban buildings is not the same as being willing to repeatedly check data, hear different views, and revise plans.

Planning work may involve meetings, field surveys, and delivery deadlines. First verify the region, travel, hours, and contract of the actual position, and do not treat US statistics or one planning institute's conditions as your own income and schedule.

First distinguish plan-making, implementation evaluation, and specialized studies; individual buildings, detailed landscape design, and surveying have their own occupational boundaries. Taking part in the same city project does not mean you can take on every specialty or hold statutory approval authority.

Use the original three-district park service coverage problem on this page; only pen and paper or a spreadsheet are needed. Recalculate for the E1 first version, the F1 population correction, and the F2 route change separately, and keep the E3 purpose record. No real resident visits, location traces, or formal planning drawings are needed.
What kind of person suits urban and regional planners?

First observe whether you are willing to verify population and distance inputs, explain the trade-offs in a plan, accept corrections, and state the unknown conditions clearly, then verify the professional training and the real position. The steps from E1 to F2 only test paper data and expression and do not prove formal planning ability.
Career exploration does not equal a hiring or registration qualification; plan-making, organization qualifications, and signing of deliverables are verified separately.

Observable signals are: asking about the data year, scope, and units before comparing options; being able to explain to a non-specialist reader why a population change alters the recommendation; and being willing to keep unfavourable results and update the charts, rather than picking only the figures that support your own plan.

If you only like renderings, find other people's interests hard to accept, or treat technical advice as directly approving a project, experience it cautiously. Planning involves repeated study, briefings, coordination, and version control; the real site conditions and statutory responsibility are determined by the position and regional rules.

Compare the covered population and the denominator change in E1/F1/F2, and record one correction and one real condition that is still unknown. If you are willing to keep explaining and revising, then look into a planning course or position with real feedback.

The US identity on this page is 19-3051.00 urban and regional planners, who study land and facility use in a jurisdiction and produce plans. Chinese territorial spatial planning has its own classification and practice system; architecture, landscape, surveying, and statutory approval are not automatically taken on just because of the job title.

First verify the source, year, units, and spatial scope of the population, parcels, roads, facilities, constraints, and plan version. Populations from different years, different coordinate systems, and straight-line versus walking distances cannot be combined directly; missing data should be marked unknown rather than filled with plausible values.

First ask whose public need is being addressed, which alternatives exist, and what the evaluation criteria are. Park service coverage is only one indicator; high coverage does not automatically prove that land is available, ecologically compliant, affordable, or fair, and the unknown constraints need to be written into the recommendation.

Outputs include the current-situation analysis, comparison of alternatives, planning drawings, indicator tables, explanatory reports, and revision records. Data, legends, and text must refer to the same version; the flow on this page is an editorial summary, and the actual deliverables follow the applicable brief and procedure.

When the population or travel conditions change, re-verify the numerator, denominator, and spatial conditions of the same indicator, then change the charts and conclusions. You cannot update only the final recommendation while keeping the old tables; the comparison results should be reproducible from the original inputs.

Communicate issues and trade-offs with architecture, transport, ecology, and economics specialists, management departments, and the public, and identify the person in charge. Public comments can influence a plan, but consultation is not treated as unanimous consent; technical advice, deliberation, and approval are separated by the actual procedure.

The US O*NET profile lists survey and analysis, plan evaluation, public communication, and map database maintenance. GIS, mapping, and office software are only tools; the availability of real materials, the statutory standards, and project authorization must be verified first, and knowing software is not the same as knowing planning.

Before delivery, verify that the drawings, text, indicators, and source versions are consistent, and keep the responses to comments and the basis for revisions. China's 2024 rules make the registered urban and rural planner who actually took part in the plan-making responsible for the deliverables they sign; a paper learner cannot claim signing authority or that a formal deliverable has been approved.

Plan-making forms alternatives from public needs and current-situation data; implementation evaluation checks deviations against the approved plan and actual changes. Both require keeping the data basis and the responses to comments, but a technical deliverable does not replace statutory approval.
Plan-making:
Identify the public need → verify the current situation and constraints → set comparison indicators → compare alternatives → coordinate comments → produce the graphic and written recommendation
Same-version drawings, indicator tables, alternative descriptions, and the basis for revisions
Implementation evaluation:
Take the approved version → set the evaluation scope → verify actual changes → calculate indicator differences → analyse the causes → submit evaluation recommendations
A comparison of plan objectives with actual changes, an explanation of deviations, and follow-up recommendations
Shared delivery conditions
Sources, periods, and spatial bases are clear; charts and text are verifiable; comments, revisions, and responsibility are recorded.
How do plan-making and implementation evaluation differ?

Plan-making focuses on future spatial arrangements and choosing among options, while evaluation focuses on whether the approved objectives were implemented and why things changed. Drawing one map cannot be treated as completing either flow, and the data and procedure boundaries must be explained together with the deliverable.
Main purpose
Compare spatial use options and put forward grounded planning recommendations.
Compare plan objectives with actual changes, and explain the deviations and follow-up recommendations.
Main inputs
The brief, population, facilities, and road network, land constraints, the higher-level plan, and public needs.
The approved plan, the current situation in the evaluation period, implementation records, same-basis indicators, and comments.
How the work is done
Survey and analysis, setting standards, comparing alternatives, coordinating comments, and producing a single-version deliverable.
Verify the baseline and actual data, calculate differences, verify the causes, then put forward traceable recommendations.
Typical outputs
Drawings, indicator tables, plan descriptions, and records of how comments were handled.
An objective and current-situation comparison, a change analysis, and evaluation recommendations.
Responsibility boundaries
The technical plan moves through the statutory procedure, with plan-making and approval responsibility verified separately.
Distinguish data changes from genuine implementation deviations, and do not declare success from one indicator.
Who to work with
Management departments, the public, and related specialties such as architecture, transport, and ecology.
The implementing body, statistical or survey providers, managers, and professional evaluators.
Do not confuse
A rendering does not prove legality or compliance, and plan-making staff do not hold approval authority because of their job title.
A change of sample or year boundary does not automatically equal a planning effect, and even less proof of causation on its own.
Key judgments in planning work

Check item by item from the public need and input quality through comparison indicators to revisions and responsibility; separate the technical conclusions that can be recalculated from the matters that require a real statutory procedure for confirmation.
Are the objectives, the affected groups, and the criteria for comparing options clear?
Are the data year, units, scope, and spatial conditions consistent?
After a population or route change, which tables, charts, and conclusions need to be updated together?
How are public comments incorporated into the plan without falsely claiming unanimous consent?

Record who raised which issue, the evidence, and the effect on the plan, and keep the different demands and the unresolved constraints. The editorial exercise needs no real visits; real comment collection is carried out under authorization, privacy, and the applicable procedure.
Who is responsible for the technical advice, signing the deliverable, and statutory approval?

Verify by the jurisdiction and the organization's duties. Chinese registration qualifications, registered practice, plan-making organization qualifications, and the approval body are not the same thing; without the corresponding status or duty, you cannot sign on someone's behalf or claim approval.
Are the delivered drawings, text, indicators, and their basis the same version and traceable?

Research | Survey and data checking | Conduct field surveys or study population, socio-economic, regulatory, and physical factors, state the period, scope, and limitations of the materials, and do not automatically fill in missing values.

Plan analysis | Comparing plans and indicators | Assess the feasibility of land and facility choices and the alternatives, explain the comparison criteria and effects, and do not rely only on a rendering or a single score.

Information maintenance | Map and database maintenance | Compile and maintain maps, databases, and statistical records, verify that the spatial basis, legends, fields, and text are consistent, and keep revised versions.

Communication and coordination | Public and professional coordination | Organize communication or meetings, respond to inquiries and different demands, coordinate with transport, architecture, and economics specialists, and do not fabricate public consensus.

Rule checking | Checking regulations and constraints | Keep track of applicable land use, zoning, building, and environmental provisions, explain the technical analysis and the management procedure, and do not substitute US rules for Chinese ones.

Deliverable explanation | Reports and implementation recommendations | Explain the planning study with reports and charts, and put forward technical advice such as approve, do not approve, or approve with conditions, or an implementation evaluation; the final authority is determined by the actual procedure.
Scenario overview | Settings for planning research, plan-making, and implementation evaluation

Document research, GIS mapping, plan discussion, and public communication often occur together. The US O*NET context survey is group background only and is not extrapolated to every Chinese workstation.

Work setting | Settings such as local government, planning and design consultancies, and research institutions, with some tasks requiring field surveys. The share of US government employers in BLS data cannot be used to calculate the Chinese job distribution.

Materials and tools | Population, land, facility, and road data, approved plans, regulation versions, map databases, and reports; GIS, CAD, and spreadsheets assist analysis, but a tool name does not equal AI capability or a practice qualification.

Organization and division of work: research, plan, specialized, and evaluation tasks are divided by public issue, with the data providers, design responsibility, comment handling, and reviewers identified; one person cannot be assumed to cover every specialty.

Scheduling | Most US planners work full time, with some evening or weekend meetings; travel, deadlines, and hours for Chinese positions are verified separately, and the survey is not treated as a uniform shift pattern.

Cooperation and feedback: discuss trade-offs with management departments and the public, and verify conditions with transport, ecology, architecture, and economics specialists; differing views and changes must keep their sources and responses.

Review method | First verify the base data and standard version, then check the indicator calculations, the consistency of charts and text, and the handling of comments. A data correction may change the recommendation, so the results must be updated, not just the description.

Delivery quality | Verifiable sources, calculations, and reasons for the alternatives are basic delivery conditions; a real statutory deliverable must comply with the applicable planning constraints and procedure. The paper service coverage problem does not prove that a formal plan is compliant or approved.
Urban and regional planners: tasks, abilities, and evidence
US 19-3051.00 land and facility plans, survey and analysis, public coordination, and map maintenance; the group IEC interest is not an individual qualification.
The BLS2025 wages and 2025—2035 projection, US work environment, and typical training; the indicators and jurisdiction are not extrapolated to China.
The specific planning position conditions at Tsinghua Tongheng and the Jiangsu Planning Group are employer samples only, not a national threshold; a quoted salary does not represent actual income.

Natural Resources Regulation [2024] No. 3 on registration access, application, registration, and signing responsibility; the old 2017 notice has been repealed and the old year limits cannot be carried over.
The ILO2025 cross-occupation potential GenAI exposure method, used only as AI interpretation background and not providing a Chinese adoption or replacement rate for this occupation.

Urban and regional planners turn land, population, transport, facility, and regulatory materials into discussable spatial plans and implementation recommendations, surveying the current situation, comparing alternatives, coordinating public comments, and keeping drawings and text consistent. It is not just drawing attractive maps: indicators, data versions, statutory procedures, and signing responsibility all have to be checked. US occupational statistics and Chinese territorial spatial planning practice conditions are explained separately.
Deliver schemes and drawings around a building's function, space, and design.
Carry out landscape design and spatial organization for sites such as parks and open spaces.
Collect, process, and present geographic information to produce maps and related spatial materials.
Study regional, natural, and human spatial distributions and their relationships, producing analyses and research outputs.
Plan-making (a direction within this occupation)
Turn the current situation, higher-level requirements, and needs into land use, facility, and spatial plans, delivering drawings, descriptions, and a comparison of alternatives.
The focus is on forming explainable spatial arrangements; a technical recommendation is not an administrative approval, and a formal deliverable still requires real review and signing.
If you are willing to repeatedly check data, draw, and explain trade-offs, first test your interest with a fictional facility siting problem.
Implementation evaluation (a direction within this occupation)
Compare plan objectives with current changes, analyse population, facility, land, and implementation problems, and deliver indicator tables, a problem list, and adjustment recommendations.
The focus is on versions, indicators, and explaining differences; one observation must not be treated as a causal conclusion or as a substitute for a formal change procedure.
If you like tracking changes, recalculating, and writing up evidence, start by checking one population and road condition update.
Architects
The main subject is the building and its design conditions; a planner's regional plan cannot replace professional architectural design and local qualifications.
If you would rather go deeper into building-scale design, you need to build architectural techniques, a portfolio, and the target position's conditions.
Landscape architects
It goes deeper into site and landscape design; regional facility siting is not the same as completed planting, grading, and construction design.
If you care about the experience of a specific open space, start with a site analysis, then verify the design training and qualification requirements.
Cartographers and photogrammetrists
The focus is the accuracy of map data and survey presentation; knowing GIS does not automatically give you the ability to be responsible for survey deliverables.
If you prefer data, remote sensing, and map quality, you need to build the target methods, precision, and real deliverable requirements.
Geographers
The focus is spatial explanation and research methods; planning experience cannot replace rigorous research design and evidence testing.
If you would rather pose spatial questions, analyse data, and explain mechanisms, start with a small study with a clear scope.
How do you choose between plan-making, implementation evaluation, and adjacent occupations?

First distinguish plan-making and implementation evaluation within this occupation, then compare separate occupations such as architecture, landscape, map data, and geographic research. Sharing spatial materials or taking part in the same project does not mean the outputs, qualifications, and responsibilities are interchangeable. The experience suggestions in the table are an editorial compilation and should be verified against the target employer and jurisdiction.

If you like forming and explaining spatial plans, try the plan-making direction first; if you like tracking indicators and actual change, try implementation evaluation first. If you lean more toward architecture, site design, map precision, or research questions, build the training and portfolio for the target occupation, and do not treat planning experience as automatically obtaining another professional qualification.

The two directions within this occupation are summarized from the O*NET 19-3051.00 tasks and the BLS work description; the four adjacent occupations each cite their separate O*NET profiles. The fit signals are editorial suggestions and cannot replace Chinese job notices, the registration system, or verification of real professional ability.
Once you have decided which output you would rather deliver long term, look at which steps AI can assist with, and at data verification, public communication, and signing responsibility.

Editorial suggestion: text tools can be used to organize the contents of public planning materials, raise comparison questions, or generate a report outline. Check the original documents and page numbers sentence by sentence, and do not let the model invent population, land indicators, policy validity, or public positions. Saving drafting time does not mean the plan is already technically feasible.

Spatial analysis should use data with a source, date, and coordinate system, and results should be checked with reproducible methods. GIS software appearing in the O*NET tools list does not mean the occupation has widely adopted generative AI; distances, coverage rates, and layer descriptions produced by a model must be verified separately.

Insufficient evidence: the national AI adoption rate, task replacement proportion, and net employment change caused by AI for urban and regional planners in China. This page reviewed occupational tasks, the ILO 2025 exposure study, the NIST framework, and recruitment samples, none of which constitutes a representative Chinese adoption survey for this occupation.

First verify the data provider, permission, confidentiality level, and the permitted processing environment. Resident comments, contact details, fine-grained traces, and unpublished project materials cannot be uploaded directly just because they would help generate a report; specific use follows the real rules of the organization and project.

Generated renderings can help discuss visual direction, but they should be marked as indicative, showing which parts were generated and which conditions are unverified. A good-looking image does not prove that building dimensions, traffic capacity, sunlight, ecological constraints, and budget hold up, and it cannot replace formal planning drawings.

China's current registered urban and rural planner system requires the relevant deliverables to be signed by the registered personnel who actually took part, who bear the prescribed responsibility. An AI draft does not obtain registration and does not turn a technical recommendation into an administrative approval; the author, the reviewer, and the approval body must be distinguished.

Summarizing public comments must preserve the original meaning, sources, and disagreements. Repeated statements, minority views, and non-digital channels must not be left out by automatic summaries; planners should explain the basis for trade-offs, and must not treat a model's summary of “consensus” as completing the statutory participation procedure.

The US 2025—2035 employment projection for this occupation shows 3.9% growth, which the OOH rounds to 4%. The projection includes factors such as demand and replacements and cannot be split into an independent AI net effect, let alone used to estimate an individual's unemployment probability in China.

The ILO 2025 study assesses potential generative AI exposure at the task level and emphasizes the possibility of occupational change. It does not provide a measured replacement rate for this occupation in China for this page; this page does not fill in a FermatMind task score that has not been established.
How will AI change planning tasks and responsibilities?

First distinguish text drafting, spatial analysis, public comments, and statutory responsibility. Tools can serve as controlled assistance, but every number, layer, policy citation, and plan judgment must be verifiable. This page has no Chinese actual adoption rate or personal replacement probability for this occupation, and does not use a general exposure study to fill in a score.

The materials below support occupational tasks, potential exposure, risk management, qualification responsibility, and the US aggregate projection respectively. They are at different source levels; this page clearly marks the methods used in planning scenarios as editorial suggestions and does not claim that these methods are already implemented nationwide.
The ILO 2025 global task-level study of potential generative AI exposure
Potential exposure does not equal actual adoption or job loss; a global study cannot be used to estimate a replacement rate for Chinese planners.
The NIST AI RMF 1.0 cross-sector artificial intelligence risk management framework
A voluntary general framework, not Chinese planning regulations or an effectiveness experiment for tools in this occupation.
Natural Resources Regulation [2024] No. 3 on the registered urban and rural planner system and examination measures
Clarifies access, registration, signing by those who actually took part, and responsibility for deliverables; AI output does not replace these conditions.
Applies within the Chinese system; it cannot be extrapolated to US registration rules, and it does not provide an AI usage rate for this occupation.
The US BLS 2025—2035 aggregate projection for urban and regional planners
Employment rises from 45.8 thousand to 47.6 thousand, growth of 3.9%; the annual average of 3.2 thousand openings includes replacements.
A US aggregate occupational projection that cannot separate an AI causal effect or represent Chinese project demand.
O*NET 19-3051.00 land, facility, survey, and public communication tasks
Used to identify the real planning tasks that involve data verification, plan comparison, and stakeholder communication.
The occupational profile is not a generative AI adoption survey; a GIS software entry does not prove an AI effect.
Can AI write the planning report directly?

An outline or text draft can be tried in an authorized environment, but the materials, years, regulations, and consistency of text and graphics must be checked item by item. The recommendations in the report are judged by people; unverified citations and numbers cannot enter a formal deliverable.
Does generating a map equal completing a spatial analysis?

No. The layer source, coordinate system, scale, connectivity, and algorithm must be verified, and key results recalculated. Roads looking connected on screen does not prove they are actually walkable, and a generated map cannot replace valid base data.
Can resident comments be uploaded directly for summarization?

First verify authorization, privacy, and project confidentiality requirements, and use the permitted processing environment. The summary must be checked for omissions and shifts in position, keeping disagreements and traceable evidence; uploading does not imply permission to publish.
Can an AI draft replace a registered signature?
Can we calculate how many planning positions AI will reduce?

This page has no causal Chinese employment data for this occupation. Potential exposure, tool requirements in recruitment, and the US aggregate projection cannot independently calculate a net job loss, nor give an individual's hiring or unemployment probability.
Can overseas frameworks be used directly as Chinese regulations?

No. The NIST framework can help design verification questions, but the actual law and organizational obligations must return to current Chinese rules and project conditions; overseas research does not grant plan-making, signing, or approval authority.
What should beginners verify first?

First complete one independent calculation with public or fictional data, listing the inputs, rules, results, and unknown conditions; then compare the errors and corrections in a tool draft. Being able to explain the results and limits is more useful than showing a generated rendering.
Occupational task profile
Identifies planning duties and tool background; it does not prove that AI works.
Task exposure research
The ILO 2025 potential exposure method and its boundaries, not a Chinese adoption rate.
Risk management framework
The general risk concepts of NIST AI RMF 1.0; the use for this occupation is an editorial suggestion.
Current qualification system
The 2024 Chinese requirements on registration, signing by those who actually took part, and responsibility.
Current examination notice
The 2026 Yantai application conditions and examination arrangements; it does not provide AI usage data.
US employment outlook
The 2025—2035 aggregate projection for this occupation, without separating an AI causal effect.
Risk management framework
Check data, output, and responsibility; it does not replace planning regulations.
Technical capability: whether the designated assistive task can be completed
Actual adoption: whether it is used in a real planning process
Employment outcome: how job demand changes
Material organization
Summarizing public policies and planning texts
An outline can be drafted
Check the original page numbers, validity, and applicable area; do not generate provisions that do not exist.
Data preparation
Checking population, facility, land use, and road layers
Field checking can be assisted
Verify the source date, units, coordinates, and gaps; a value the model fills in cannot be assumed to be real.
Plan comparison
Calculating candidate facility coverage and alternative routes
Independent recalculation is required
Keep the threshold, denominator, and algorithm, and check how a change affects the conclusion.

Organizing interviews and feedback by topic
A controlled summary can be tried
First verify processing authorization, then check the positions, minority views, and omissions against the original.
Visual discussion
Producing indicative images of the plan
Clear generation labelling
Distinguish image presentation from engineering conditions, and do not claim that capacity, budget, or approval has been established.
Deliverable review
Checking charts, text, and higher-level requirements
Error checking assistance
The actual participants and reviewers verify and fulfil the signing responsibility, and tools are not allowed to sign on their behalf.
Career choice
Comparing tool requirements, position tasks, and demand
Net employment impact not quantified
Check real positions and time series, and do not treat individual AI positions as a national adoption rate.
Text and materials
Outlines and summaries may change the drafting process; efficiency was not measured on this page.
Responsible for checking the original policy text, the sources of figures, and omissions in the summary.
Spatial and visual
Computational assistance and renderings have different verification requirements, and generation speed alone is not enough.
Responsible for data quality, recalculating results, and labelling indicative images.
Participation and responsibility
Organizing comments can be assisted; technical advice, registered signing, and approval still each have their own responsible party.
Explain the trade-offs in the plan, record disagreements, and fulfil the actual duties.
Define the task first
Clarify whether the job is to organize policy, verify data, or compare plans, and write down the acceptance deliverable and the conclusions that must not be extrapolated.
Verify material permissions
Confirm the data source, permission, privacy, and the organization's permitted environment; verify unpublished materials with the project lead first.
Independently verify results
Check the citations and data, recalculate the key indicators; record the errors and unverified conditions, and do not rely on the model's self-assessment.
Assign responsibility
Distinguish drafting, technical review, registered signing, and administrative approval; the actual participants bear responsibility under the current rules.
Keep the changes
Record the tool, inputs, version, and human revisions; for public comments keep the differing positions and the basis for how they were handled.
Fabricated policies and data
The plan rests on provisions that do not exist or on a wrong population.
Check the original basis and data version item by item; a generated citation cannot verify itself.
Coordinate and scale errors
Distorted facility distances, areas, and covered subjects.
Verify the coordinate system and units, and spot-check key distances with an independent method.
Distorted comment summaries
Minority or opposing views are treated as support.
Check the original text and the collection channel, keep the disagreements, and do not manufacture public consensus.
Data leaks
Resident privacy or unpublished project materials enter an unauthorized environment.
Verify permissions and the confidentiality level, use the approved environment, and limit the data scope.
Indicative images passed off as deliverables
Images are mistaken for verified buildability, approval, or a signature.
Mark it as indicative and note the unknown conditions; a formal deliverable goes through the real plan-making and review procedure.
Career explorers
First do the fictional coverage exercise, then check whether a generated explanation omits the denominator or presents a learning threshold as a statutory standard.
Students
Build a public source list and an independent recalculation record; the work sample states your own, the tool's, and collaborators' contributions, and unauthorized projects are not uploaded.
Working planners
Pick one low-sensitivity assistive task to test, and record the errors, corrections, and who reviewed it; a tool suggestion does not replace signing responsibility.
Project leads
Clarify the permitted materials, verification methods, and public labelling; public participation, data handling, and formal deliverables all follow the real project rules.

Insufficient evidence: the national exact occupational wage distribution for urban and regional planners in mainland China. The specific planning positions at Tsinghua Tongheng, the Jiangsu Planning Group spring recruitment, and the CAUPD notice were checked; position samples with quotes or no amount listed cannot form a national percentile distribution.

First verify whether it is a formal employee or internship status, an annual package or monthly wage, fixed versus performance pay, the probation period, work location, and hours; a notice's range is not a take-home guarantee, and an internship monthly allowance cannot be compared directly with a formal annual salary.

A project contract amount in planning consultancy is not the same as personal income. Fees also involve team, data, travel, and delivery costs, and this page does not infer a planner's net wage from project size or a quote.

The Tsinghua Tongheng Henan Branch J10912 notice dated 2026-04-07 quotes 10—20 ten-thousand yuan per year, with conditions such as 2—5 years of experience, a bachelor's degree or above in the field, and an intermediate professional title; the Beijing J10942 internship dated 2026-06-18 quotes 2K—3K yuan per month. Both positions are with the same employer and are not two independent industry statistics.

The Jiangsu Planning Group spring recruitment notice dated 2026-05-09 runs to May 22, and the application period has passed. The Nanjing meso and micro campus recruitment requires a master's degree in urban and rural planning; the Chengdu campus recruitment requires a master's degree, and the experienced hire route a bachelor's degree and 3 years of experience, with no wage listed this time, and a conditions table is not filled in as income.
Planner pay in China: formal annual salaries, internship quotes, and the national gap

Employer quotes | Tsinghua Tongheng Henan Branch planning designer J10912: 10 ten-thousand to 20 ten-thousand yuan per year, published 2026-04-07; Beijing general development research and planning branch J10942 internship: 2,000—3,000 yuan per month, published 2026-06-18. Not statistics of actual take-home pay.

Insufficient evidence: the specific wage amounts for the planning positions in the Jiangsu Planning Group 2026 spring recruitment. This round read the field, education, and experience conditions, and the notice lists no amount; the Tsinghua Tongheng pay is not applied.

Zhengzhou J10912 is a formal experienced-hire sample, requiring 2—5 years of planning experience, an intermediate professional title, and a bachelor's degree or above in urban and rural planning, with a postgraduate degree and registration preferred; 10 ten-thousand to 20 ten-thousand yuan per year does not equal the national distribution for the same years of experience.

Beijing J10942 is an internship sample covering assistance with plan-making, deliverables, research topics, drawing, databases, and field surveys, quoted at 2,000—3,000 yuan per month; it cannot be used to infer a formal planner's monthly wage or the national newcomer level.

The Jiangsu Group Nanjing meso and micro campus recruitment sample requires a master's degree in urban and rural planning and drawing standards ability, while the Chengdu direction distinguishes campus and experienced-hire routes; no specific wage is listed and the spring recruitment application period has closed.

The national exact wage distribution remains a gap; employer quotes, internship quotes, and US statistics are interpreted by their own period, status, and region, and are not combined into a single income range.

Verify the fixed wage, performance pay conditions, probation period, overtime and travel, social insurance, and the contracting entity; a project budget and income are not directly the same, and a notice's upper figure does not guarantee payment each period.

Insufficient evidence: comparable data on wage changes for urban and regional planners in China after AI adoption. The Jiangsu Group's separate AI product architect position does not mean planners have widely adopted AI or taken pay cuts; the actual tasks, hours, quality, and pay need verification.

Position quotes keep their original annual or monthly unit, internships and formal jobs are not mixed, and the Jiangsu spring recruitment has expired; a small number of employer samples cannot represent national wages for this occupation, and software proficiency certainly cannot be used to infer take-home income.

The 2025 US median wage for 19-3051 urban and regional planners is 89,320 US dollars per year and 42.94 US dollars per hour. Both units keep the original BLS values cited by O*NET, and no personal after-tax income is inferred.
The 10th percentile is 60,010 US dollars per year and 28.85 US dollars per hour, a lower position in the distribution, not the wage of all new hires or a minimum guarantee.
The 90th percentile is 134,490 US dollars per year and 64.66 US dollars per hour, which does not equal a uniform senior pay grade or a ceiling an individual will necessarily reach.

The EMP2025—2035 projection is 45,800 to 47,600 people, with 3.9% in the original table (the OOH rounds to 4%), and an annual average of 3,200 openings including replacements for people leaving, which is not 3,200 net additions each year.

OEWS wages cover wage and salary employees and exclude the self-employed; the EMP employment projection has its own coverage. Wages and headcount cannot be multiplied to infer personal or industry net income.

The original table gives both the annual and the hourly figures, so both are kept, and the annual value is not recalculated from 2,080 hours; actual paid hours, benefits and taxes, and employment conditions are verified separately.
US urban and regional planner wages and employment: 2025 official basis
2025 national wage percentiles: annual and hourly
The median is the middle position of the employee wage distribution; it is not a Chinese quote for the same position and does not guarantee an individual's annual hours or take-home monthly wage.
How do you distinguish statistical wages from actual personal income?
A percentile is a position in the distribution and does not map to years of work, registration, or a promotion level; P25 is not a bachelor's degree wage and P75 is not a master's degree wage.
First verify employee or self-employed status, fixed or variable pay, hours, benefits, and work location; a total project consultancy contract cannot be treated as one planner's annual wage.
2025 major industries: median annual wages for this occupation
The annual median for this occupation in architectural, engineering, and related services is 102,740 US dollars; this is not the wage of all engineers in that industry.
The annual median for this occupation in state government excluding education and hospitals is 91,060 US dollars, which cannot be extrapolated to Chinese public institutions.
The annual median for this occupation in local government excluding education and hospitals is 85,980 US dollars, which differs from private consultancy project fees.

There is also an annual median of 93,220 US dollars for this occupation in management, scientific, and technical consulting; these are all employee statistics and exclude self-employed net income. A personal consultancy needs separately verifying turnover, costs, and time.
What other conditions are needed to compare positions?

values: E1 | fictional park candidate coverage exercise
Three district populations: P300 people, Q200 people, and R100 people, 600 in total. Walking distances: A→P300 metres, Q700 metres, R450 metres; B→P650 metres, Q250 metres, R400 metres.

Choose only one candidate, A or B; rule: if the distance is ≤500 metres, the whole district population counts, and each person is counted once. Coverage = counted population ÷ the total population for that version × 100%, keeping 1 decimal place. Recommend by the largest covered population; the 500 metres is only a learning assumption, not a statutory standard, and the problem gives no cost, capacity, land, or real roads.
E2 / E3 | your task and the two rounds of feedback

E1 first calculates A and B separately. F1 corrects only the Q population of 200 to 500, leaving everything else unchanged, and recalculates both candidates. F2, building on F1, changes the B→R distance of 400 to 750 metres (route closed), keeping the other distances and populations as in F1; recalculate and explain whether the recommendation changes.

E3 states: a fictional problem for this page, your own input table and calculation, and F1/F2 as the given feedback; no real residents, plots, or interviews. Record the purpose and differences of each version, list the unknown cost, capacity, regulations, and route authenticity, and do not fabricate third-party support.
Reference answers | numerator, denominator, and changes
E1: A counts P+R = 400 people, 400/600 = 66.7%; B counts Q+R = 300 people, 300/600 = 50.0%, so the single indicator chooses A. F1 total 900 people: A400/900 = 44.4%; B600/900 = 66.7%, choosing B.

F2 total still 900 people: A400/900 = 44.4%; B counts only Q500/900 = 55.6%, so B is still chosen. B has 100 fewer people than F1 and falls by 11.1 percentage points; an unchanged recommendation does not mean the data are unchanged. This can only support that fictional single-indicator comparison and cannot claim that a real park is buildable or that residents are satisfied.
Exercise boundaries | pen and paper are enough

No GIS, site visits, or real resident information are needed. Calculate independently from the given distances, do not treat them as straight-line distances or fill in capacity, calculate each candidate separately, and do not add the two coverages together. The problem does not prove fairness, the real route, lawful land use, funding, or approval.

Which tasks new graduates and career changers should verify first

The stages below are organized by ability and evidence, not uniform job grades or automatic promotion years. The real division of work, employer conditions, and Chinese registered signing responsibility are verified separately; a learning work sample cannot replace a formal project or qualification.
Chinese qualifications / US background applied separately
2026 employer condition samples:

China's current system is an access-type qualification; after obtaining the qualification and registering according to law, you practise within the scope of the system, and the relevant deliverables are signed by the registered personnel who actually took part. Can verify materials

Can calculate and explain
Recalculates indicators, compares alternatives, explains the rules and limits, and accepts factual corrections.
Can maintain changes
Keeps data, drawings, and text in step, and records version differences and review comments.
Can organize complex sub-packages

Basic materials assistant

Adds a short analysis of public materials and records the specific revisions made after comments.

Can explain the choices, changes, and review records for one sub-package, not just show renderings.
Signing Chinese deliverables is the responsibility of the registered personnel who actually took part, under the system.
Build cost, regulatory, spatial design, and communication ability, and verify the real division of work before expanding tasks.
Complex project collaboration
Coordinates multiple spatial issues and specialist opinions, and clarifies the boundary between technical advice and approval.
Has traceable evidence of plan comparison, issue handling, and your own contribution.
Personal registration, organization qualifications, and competent department approval are verified separately, without borrowing names or signing on others' behalf.
Deepens the target specialty or project coordination, without promising a lead grade based on years.
Implementation evaluation and plan adjustment recommendations
Current-situation update
Verify the data time and basis, and organize pre- and post-implementation materials and gaps.
Input versions, sources, and comparability are clear, and non-comparable items are clearly marked.
Position conditions are verified separately, and the learning problem is not an official evaluation.
Build statistics, indicator definitions, and public material verification.

Compares changes under consistent rules, distinguishing factual corrections from real changes in conditions.

Correlation must not be treated as causation, and the results are subject to review in a real project.
Try comparing public data versions, keeping the method and the unknowns.
Evaluation recommendations and communication
Turn implementation problems, alternative measures, and limitations into a clear report, and check the views of multiple parties.
Has a correspondence between evidence and recommendations, and keeps the disagreements and unverified conditions.
Technical advice is not the same as a formal plan amendment or administrative approval.
Build evaluation methods, regulations, and participatory communication.

Coordinates multi-specialty data and explains budget, environmental, and public need constraints.
Has records of data traceability, recalculation, review, and your own responsibility.
Formal deliverables, registered signing, and change procedures follow the actual system.
Deepens implementation evaluation or the corresponding specialty, without using a single indicator to prove overall success.

Survey preparation
Clarify the question, the permitted materials, and the collection channel, and organize existing materials under guidance.
Sources, scope, and materials that cannot be collected are listed clearly, and no survey is fabricated.
Real resident materials are handled according to privacy, permission, and organizational requirements.
Start with fictional or public data, and build basic survey methods.

Records feedback, distinguishing facts, preferences, and items to be verified, and checks for omissions.
Original meaning, disagreements, and sources are traceable, and a summary is not treated as consensus.
Verify the real participation procedure and material permissions; AI cannot confirm authorization.
Build training in interviews, questionnaires, and information synthesis.

Clearly explains the basis of the plan and records the question, who replied, and the revision status.
Differing views are not lost, changes go into charts and text, and open questions are traceable.
Makes no budget, approval, or implementation promises beyond authority.
Build public presentation and multi-specialty collaboration, and verify the real meeting conditions.
Taking part in coordination and technical interfaces
Organizes problem classification and specialist replies, and presents the trade-offs to the real decision-makers.
Can explain your own contribution, how comments were handled, and what remains unresolved.
Organizing communication is not administrative approval or automatic signing authority.

The US BLS projects 3.9% employment growth for this occupation from 2025 to 2035, shown as 4% in the OOH; the annual average of 3,200 openings includes replacements for people leaving and changing roles and cannot be treated as 3,200 new positions each year.

BLS mentions demand for community land, facility, and development planning, and also notes that government budgets affect positions. The aggregate projection cannot show that every city, organization, or the Chinese market grows in step, and certainly cannot separate out an independent AI effect.

China's Natural Resources Regulation [2024] No. 3 defines registered urban and rural planner access, registration, and signing responsibility; the 2026 examination notice continues the corresponding application conditions. The system describes professional boundaries and does not prove recruitment numbers or pay growth.

Insufficient evidence: the current nationally representative recruitment scale, demand change, and continuous time series for this occupation in China. The 2026 Tsinghua Tongheng sample distinguishes the Zhengzhou experienced-hire position from the Beijing internship; the Jiangsu Group May notice includes planning positions in Nanjing and Chengdu, and applications have closed. A small number of notices cannot be used to estimate national demand.

Editorial judgment: survey precision and methods

subject.name: Urban and regional planners
subject.summary: Urban and regional planners turn land, population, transport, facility, and regulatory materials into discussable spatial plans and implementation recommendations, surveying the current situation, comparing alternatives, coordinating public comments, and keeping drawings and text consistent. It is not just drawing attractive maps: indicators, data versions, statutory procedures, and signing responsibility all have to be checked. US occupational statistics and Chinese territorial spatial planning practice conditions are explained separately.
